# Data table — M3 guidance

<!-- Generated by apps/site/scripts/one-off/migrate-guidance.mjs. Do not edit by hand.
     The component pages carry the reference; this file carries the guidance. -->

## Web

### Features

Reach for the data table when the content is a grid that sorts, pages and selects: one controlled grid over columns and rows with four presets in `variant`. The preset picks density, sticky header, selection and row actions in one choice — admin-grid, bookings, ledger, csv-preview — and `density`, `stickyHeader` and `selectable` override it per table. The ledger and csv-preview presets drop selection and row actions by design: a financial grid and a preview must not start workflows. Cell kinds are text, numeric, status and actions with a custom `render` per column, `query` is the global text filter owned by the search above the table rather than by the table, and row actions live in an overflow menu per row, so they never steal the row's own activation. Sortable headers expose their order on the header itself, the header select-all reports the indeterminate state when some page rows are selected, and a real caption names the table. The host owns columns, rows, sort, page and selection throughout — the table fetches nothing.

## Native

### Features

Reach for the data table when the content is a grid that sorts, pages and selects: one controlled grid over columns and rows with four presets in `variant` — the native twin under the same contract. The preset picks density, sticky header, selection and row actions in one choice — admin-grid, bookings, ledger, csv-preview — and `density`, `stickyHeader` and `selectable` override it per table. The ledger and csv-preview presets drop selection and row actions by design: a financial grid and a preview must not start workflows. Native renders list-cards under the shared contract — one card per row with label-and-value lines — with a sort header row reporting direction on each sortable column, per-row selection and row actions, and page controls announcing as table pages with the current window labelled. The host owns columns, rows, sort, page and selection throughout — the table fetches nothing.
